# Model and source

Su et al. developed a multiscale mechanistic cellular-kinetic / pharmacodynamic
(CK-PD) framework for **dual-targeted bicistronic CAR T-cell therapy**, in which
a single T cell expresses two independent chimeric-antigen receptors. The paper
builds the framework in two layers and validates it on two antigen pairs:

1. An *in vitro* cell-level tumour-killing model (Figure 1a) in which CAR T cells
   and tumour cells coexist in a culture well, the two CARs form single- and
   double-target complexes, and complexes per tumour cell drive Emax killing.
   It is fit to CD19/CD22 CAR-T co-cultured with B-cell ALL cell lines and
   validated on an independent GPRC5D/BCMA CAR-T multiple-myeloma dataset whose
   two co-stimulatory-domain designs are compared.
2. An *in vivo* clinical CK-PD model (Figure 1b) that embeds the same binding and
   killing mechanism in a two-compartment (peripheral blood + bone marrow)
   cellular-kinetic structure with effector/memory phenotype transformation, and
   fits it to the phase 1 CD19/CD22 CAR-T (AUTO3) dose-escalation study in
   pediatric and young-adult B-ALL.

This article packages four model files from the paper:

```{r models}
mod_clin <- readModelDb("Su_2025_cd19cd22cart_ALL")
mod_vitro_ball <- readModelDb("Su_2025_cd19cd22cart_invitro")
mod_vitro_41bb <- readModelDb("Su_2025_gprc5dbcmacart_41BB_invitro")
mod_vitro_cd28 <- readModelDb("Su_2025_gprc5dbcmacart_CD28_invitro")
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(mod_clin)$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13259>
* Supporting information (equations, Monolix model code, datasets):
  <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13259> (PMC11812944 open-access package)

# Population

The clinical model was fit to the phase 1 dose-escalation study of the
CD19/CD22 dual-targeted CAR-T product AUTO3 (Cordoba et al. 2021, Nat Med
27:1797-1805) in 14 pediatric and young-adult patients (age 4-16) with relapsed
or refractory B-cell ALL, who received a single infusion of 0.3-2, 3 or
5 x 10^6 CAR+ T cells/kg. Fourteen patients contributed 157 qPCR samples and
five mapped patients contributed 43 flow-cytometry samples. The model accounts
for each product's memory/effector phenotypic composition (cohort mean
0.86:0.13), individual baseline CD19 and CD22 tumour-antigen densities, and
age-based body weight, assuming a 1:1 ratio of CD4+ to CD8+ CAR T cells.

```{r population}
mod_clin()$population[c("species", "n_subjects", "age_range", "disease_state", "dose_range")]
```

# Source trace

Per-parameter origins are recorded as in-file comments next to each `ini()`
entry in each model file under `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/`. The clinical
equations are Supplement 1 Eqs. 15-52 with the as-run Monolix code of
Supplement 2; the in-vitro equations are Supplement 1 Eqs. 1-14. Parameter
values are main-text Table 1.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source |
|----------------------|-------|--------|
| KMaxExp (max effector expansion) | 2.04 /day | Table 1, clinical |
| EC50Exp (complexes/CAR-T for half-max expansion) | 42.1 | Table 1, clinical |
| KMaxKill (max tumour kill, clinical) | 0.58 /day | Table 1, clinical |
| KC50Kill (complexes/tumour for half-max kill) | 3.57 | Table 1, clinical (fixed, in-vitro estimate) |
| Kelm / Kele (memory / effector elimination) | 0.015 / 113 /day | Table 1, clinical |
| K12 / K21 (blood<->marrow) | 2.91 / 0.18 /day | Table 1, clinical |
| Rm (net effector->memory conversion) | 2e-5 /day | Table 1, clinical (fixed) |
| KcarryTumor (tumour carrying capacity) | 0.39 x 10^10 cells/L | Table 1, clinical |
| DTTumor / Kmigration | 10.7 day / 0.001 /day | Table 1, clinical |
| Kon / Kd (CD19, CD22) | 1e5 /M/s; 1.09, 32 nM | Table 1, clinical (fixed) |
| Ag_CAR density (CD19, CD22) | 15000 /cell | Table 1, clinical (fixed) |
| alpha / beta (qPCR-flow regression) | 4.45 / 1.41 | Table 1, clinical (fixed) |
| Baseline CD19 / CD22 tumour density (cohort mean) | 16666 / 4269 /cell | Table 1, clinical |
| ICTumorPB / ICTumorBM | 1.8e9 / 1.6e11 cells/L | Table 1, clinical (fixed) |
| In-vitro B-ALL: KMaxKill / KC50 | 0.8 /day / 3.57 | Table 1, cell-level B-ALL |
| In-vitro MM 41BB (G4B4): KMaxKill / KC50 / gamma | 4.39 / 11.8 / 0.69 | Table 1, cell-level MM |
| In-vitro MM CD28 (GCB4): KMaxKill / KC50 / gamma | 2.71 / 2.38 / 1 | Table 1, cell-level MM |
| ODE systems (binding, kinetics, tumour) | n/a | Supplement 1 Eqs. 1-52 |

# Clinical CK-PD model: cellular-kinetic profiles

The model reproduces the four phases of CAR-T exposure (distribution, expansion,
contraction, persistence). We solve the typical-value model (`zeroRe`) across the
dose levels of Figure 5a. Because the blood and bone-marrow volumes both scale
with body weight and the dose is per kg, body weight cancels from every output;
the profiles below are therefore age-invariant (the model's AGE covariate is
carried for completeness).

```{r clin-typical}
mod_tv <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_clin)

# Dose in CAR+ T cells/kg, split into memory/effector pools by the cohort-mean
# product composition (0.87:0.13). The model's f(cartm_pb)/f(carte_pb) = wt/Vb
# converts cells/kg to the blood concentration, so we dose the per-kg numbers.
dose_levels <- c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 3, 5, 10) * 1e6
mem_frac <- 0.87
eff_frac <- 0.13

solve_dose <- function(d, tmax = 28, dt = 0.25, age = 10) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = d * mem_frac, cmt = "cartm_pb")
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = d * eff_frac, cmt = "carte_pb")
  # Observe the `cells` endpoint; rxode2 returns both the `cells` and
  # `transgene` outputs as columns from a multi-endpoint model.
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, seq(0, tmax, by = dt), cmt = "cells")
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tv, ev, params = c(AGE = age), method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-9, rtol = 1e-9))
  s$dose <- d
  s
}

sim_tv <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(dose_levels, solve_dose))
sim_tv$dose_lbl <- factor(paste0(sim_tv$dose / 1e6, " x10^6"),
  levels = paste0(dose_levels / 1e6, " x10^6")
)
```

```{r figure-5a}
# Replicates Figure 5a of Su 2025: CAR-T cell concentration in peripheral blood
# across dose levels.
sim_tv |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, cells, colour = dose_lbl)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "CAR-T cells (cells/uL)",
    colour = "Dose (cells/kg)",
    title = "Figure 5a - CAR-T cellular kinetics by dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5a of Su 2025."
  )
```

# Clinical CK-PD model: exposure vs. Table S3

Table S3 reports the simulated C~max~, T~max~ and AUC~0-28~ of the CAR-T
cell-count and qPCR-transgene profiles across dose levels. We reproduce those
exposure metrics with PKNCA and compare them to the published values. The
agreement is a direct check that the structural model and all fixed and
estimated parameters were transcribed correctly.

```{r pknca-cells}
# Fine grid to resolve Cmax/Tmax; 0-28 day window for AUC0-28.
sim_s3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(dose_levels, solve_dose, tmax = 28, dt = 0.1))
sim_s3$dose_lbl <- paste0(sim_s3$dose / 1e6, " x10^6")

# --- CAR-T cell-count output ---
conc_cells <- sim_s3 |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(cells)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = dose / 1e5, time, conc = cells, dose_lbl)
conc_cells <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_cells,
  conc_cells |> dplyr::distinct(id, dose_lbl) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

ivals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 28, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_cells <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_cells, conc ~ time | dose_lbl + id),
  intervals = ivals
))

# --- qPCR transgene output ---
conc_tg <- sim_s3 |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(transgene)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = dose / 1e5, time, conc = transgene, dose_lbl)
nca_tg <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_tg, conc ~ time | dose_lbl + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 28, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))

summ <- function(nca) {
  as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
    dplyr::select(dose_lbl, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
}
sim_cells <- summ(nca_cells)
sim_tg <- summ(nca_tg)
```

```{r s3-table}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_lbl, ~cmax_cell, ~tmax_cell, ~auc_cell, ~cmax_tg, ~tmax_tg, ~auc_tg,
  "0.1 x10^6", 202, 13, 2025, 152823, 13, 1271239,
  "0.5 x10^6", 208, 12, 2116, 159107, 12, 1335184,
  "1 x10^6", 210, 11, 2151, 160755, 11, 1356919,
  "3 x10^6", 242, 11, 2525, 197008, 11, 1677898,
  "5 x10^6", 266, 11, 2826, 224292, 11, 1949652,
  "10 x10^6", 313, 10, 3393, 282504, 10, 2488055
)

cmp <- published |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim_cells |> dplyr::transmute(dose_lbl, sim_cmax_cell = cmax, sim_tmax_cell = tmax, sim_auc_cell = auclast),
    by = "dose_lbl"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim_tg |> dplyr::transmute(dose_lbl, sim_cmax_tg = cmax, sim_auc_tg = auclast),
    by = "dose_lbl"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `Cmax cell %diff` = round(100 * (sim_cmax_cell - cmax_cell) / cmax_cell, 1),
    `AUC cell %diff` = round(100 * (sim_auc_cell - auc_cell) / auc_cell, 1),
    `Cmax transgene %diff` = round(100 * (sim_cmax_tg - cmax_tg) / cmax_tg, 1),
    `AUC transgene %diff` = round(100 * (sim_auc_tg - auc_tg) / auc_tg, 1)
  )

cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dose = dose_lbl,
    `Cmax cell (pub)` = cmax_cell, `Cmax cell (sim)` = round(sim_cmax_cell),
    `Tmax cell (pub)` = tmax_cell, `Tmax cell (sim)` = round(sim_tmax_cell),
    `AUC0-28 cell (pub)` = auc_cell, `AUC0-28 cell (sim)` = round(sim_auc_cell),
    `Cmax cell %diff`, `AUC cell %diff`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table S3a (cell-count): simulated vs. published CAR-T exposure.")

cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dose = dose_lbl,
    `Cmax tg (pub)` = cmax_tg, `Cmax tg (sim)` = round(sim_cmax_tg),
    `AUC0-28 tg (pub)` = auc_tg, `AUC0-28 tg (sim)` = round(sim_auc_tg),
    `Cmax transgene %diff`, `AUC transgene %diff`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table S3a (transgene): simulated vs. published CAR-T exposure.")
```

```{r s3-check}
# Structural check: the reproduced exposure metrics track the published values.
# A mis-transcribed rate constant, dose split or unit conversion would move
# these by tens of percent. The comparison is a deterministic typical-value
# reproduction (same parameters both sides), so the centre is tight; the
# loosest single point is the lowest-dose transgene Cmax, where the fixed
# log-log regression slope (1.41) amplifies the ~4% cell-level offset.
all_diffs <- c(
  cmp$`Cmax cell %diff`, cmp$`AUC cell %diff`,
  cmp$`Cmax transgene %diff`, cmp$`AUC transgene %diff`
)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(all_diffs)) < 3, # centre: structural fidelity
  max(abs(all_diffs)) < 8 # envelope across all dose levels and both outputs
)
```

# Clinical CK-PD model: population variability (Figure 6a)

The population simulation of Figure 6a overlays the low and high dose levels with
between-subject variability on the expansion, elimination, distribution and
killing rate constants. We draw a cohort of 100 subjects per dose arm (well
within the 200/arm guideline).

```{r figure-6a}
set.seed(1234)
n_arm <- 100
pop_dose <- function(d, id_offset) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = d * mem_frac, cmt = "cartm_pb")
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = d * eff_frac, cmt = "carte_pb")
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, seq(0, 28, by = 0.5), cmt = "cells")
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_clin, ev, params = c(AGE = 10),
    nSub = n_arm, method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-8, rtol = 1e-8
  ))
  s$id <- s$sim.id + id_offset
  s$dose_lbl <- paste0(d / 1e6, " x10^6")
  s
}
sim_pop <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pop_dose(0.1e6, 0L),
  pop_dose(10e6, 1000L)
)

sim_pop |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_lbl, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = median(cells), lo = quantile(cells, 0.025), hi = quantile(cells, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med, colour = dose_lbl, fill = dose_lbl)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "CAR-T cells (cells/uL)", colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
    title = "Figure 6a - population simulation, low vs high dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6a of Su 2025 (median and 95% interval)."
  )
```

# In-vitro cell-level killing: B-ALL (Figure 2)

The in-vitro model seeds tumour and CAR T cells into a culture well and reads
tumour-cell viability relative to the non-transduced control. We reproduce the
RajiWT panel of Figure 2d: non-transduced T cells (NT), the single-targeted CD19
CAR (FMC63) and the dual-targeted AUTO3. The non-targeting CAR is represented by
a near-zero association rate with the dissociation constant set high, exactly as
the authors parameterised the control arms.

```{r vitro-ball}
mod_ball <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_vitro_ball)

solve_vitro <- function(mod, dens = list(), et_ratio = 1, tumor0 = 1e5, tmax = 3) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = tumor0, cmt = "n_tumor")
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, amt = et_ratio * tumor0, cmt = "n_cart")
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, seq(0, tmax, by = 0.05))
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = unlist(dens), method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-9, rtol = 1e-9))
}

raji <- list(dens_cd19_tumor = 50347, dens_cd22_tumor = 55116)
treatments <- list(
  NT = c(raji, list(kon_orig_cd19 = 1e-10, kon_orig_cd22 = 1e-10, kd_cd19 = 1e10, kd_cd22 = 1e10)),
  `CD19 CAR (FMC63)` = c(raji, list(kon_orig_cd19 = 207622, kon_orig_cd22 = 1e-10, kd_cd19 = 0.328, kd_cd22 = 1e10)),
  `CD19/CD22 CAR (AUTO3)` = raji
)

sim_ball <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(treatments), function(tx) {
  s <- solve_vitro(mod_ball, dens = treatments[[tx]])
  s$treatment <- tx
  s
}))
sim_ball$treatment <- factor(sim_ball$treatment, levels = names(treatments))

sim_ball |>
  ggplot(aes(time, viability, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumour viability (% of control)", colour = "Treatment",
    title = "Figure 2d - RajiWT killing by CAR-T treatment",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2d of Su 2025 (RajiWT, 1:1 ET ratio)."
  )

# Non-transduced control does not kill; the CAR-T arms do (RajiWT bears both
# antigens, so single-CD19 and dual AUTO3 both clear the line).
v24 <- sapply(names(treatments), function(tx) {
  s <- solve_vitro(mod_ball, dens = treatments[[tx]], tmax = 1)
  s$viability[nrow(s)]
})
stopifnot(v24[["NT"]] > 95, v24[["CD19/CD22 CAR (AUTO3)"]] < 70)
```

# In-vitro cell-level killing: GPRC5D/BCMA, two co-stimulatory designs (Figure 3)

The independent multiple-myeloma dataset compares two bicistronic GPRC5D/BCMA
constructs with distinct co-stimulatory domains. The CD28/41BB design (GCB4)
estimated a superior potency (KC50 = 2.38 complexes/tumour cell) over the
matched-41BB design (KC50 = 11.8), while the matched-41BB design has the higher
maximum killing rate (KMaxKill = 4.39 vs. 2.71). We reproduce the
cytotoxicity-vs-effector:target curves (Figure 3) on three cell lines and
overlay the digitised observed means.

```{r vitro-mm}
cell_dens <- list(
  RPMI8226 = list(dens_bcma_tumor = 12590, dens_gprc5d_tumor = 1184),
  OPM2WT = list(dens_bcma_tumor = 5000, dens_gprc5d_tumor = 746),
  MM1S = list(dens_bcma_tumor = 4300, dens_gprc5d_tumor = 746)
)
et_grid <- c(0, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1)

mm_curve <- function(mod, label) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(cell_dens), function(cl) {
    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(et_grid, function(et) {
      s <- solve_vitro(mod, dens = cell_dens[[cl]], et_ratio = et, tumor0 = 2e4, tmax = 1)
      data.frame(cell = cl, et = et, cytotox = 100 - s$viability[nrow(s)], construct = label)
    }))
  }))
}

mm <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  mm_curve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_vitro_41bb), "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB"),
  mm_curve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_vitro_cd28), "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB")
)

# Digitised observed cytotoxicity means (Supplement 3 datasets).
mm_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~construct, ~cell, ~et, ~cytotox,
  "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 0.03, 31.34, "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 0.1, 70.03,
  "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 0.3, 89.37, "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 1, 98.91,
  "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 0.03, 45.98, "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 0.1, 54.02,
  "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 0.3, 63.19, "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 1, 79.69,
  "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 0.03, 9.61, "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 0.1, 22.20,
  "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 0.3, 53.39, "GPRC5D-41BB-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 1, 87.87,
  "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 0.03, 43.05, "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 0.1, 49.86,
  "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 0.3, 77.79, "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "RPMI8226", 1, 92.23,
  "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 0.03, 46.54, "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 0.1, 59.10,
  "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 0.3, 71.51, "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "OPM2WT", 1, 88.29,
  "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 0.03, 8.03, "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 0.1, 32.76,
  "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 0.3, 59.06, "GPRC5D-CD28-BCMA-41BB", "MM1S", 1, 93.23
)

ggplot(mm, aes(et, cytotox, colour = construct)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = mm_obs, aes(et, cytotox, colour = construct), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~cell) +
  labs(
    x = "Effector : target ratio", y = "Cytotoxicity (% of control)",
    colour = "Construct",
    title = "Figure 3 - GPRC5D/BCMA cytotoxicity by co-stimulatory design",
    caption = "Lines: model; open points: digitised observed means. Replicates Figure 3 of Su 2025."
  )

# Cytotoxicity rises monotonically with effector:target ratio for every
# construct x cell line (a structural property of the killing model).
mono <- mm |>
  dplyr::arrange(construct, cell, et) |>
  dplyr::group_by(construct, cell) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ok = all(diff(cytotox) > 0), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(mono$ok))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Two outputs link by a fixed regression.** The qPCR transgene output is a
  fixed log-log function of the flow CAR-T cell count
  (`ln(transgene) = 4.45 + 1.41 * ln(cells/uL)`); both intercept and slope were
  fixed by the authors, so the two outputs carry the same information up to the
  transform.
- **Residual error recovered from the goodness-of-fit figures.** Table 1 does not
  tabulate the residual-error magnitudes. The maintainers recovered them from the
  Monolix observations-vs-individual-predictions panels of Figure S2 by reading
  the 90% prediction-interval offsets: the qPCR output is proportional
  (SD = 0.73, from the censored-point band in Figure S2a/S2d), and the flow
  output is a combined additive-plus-proportional error
  (SD = 2.1 cells/uL + 0.54, from Figure S2b/S2f). These affect only the width of
  a simulated prediction interval, not the typical-value exposure predictions
  validated against Table S3.
- **Baseline antigen densities are encoded at the cohort averages.** The clinical
  model reads per-patient baseline CD19 (16666, range 1324-39098) and CD22 (4269,
  range 181-10137) tumour-antigen densities as inputs. They are encoded here as
  fixed parameters set to the cohort averages and are overridable per patient
  (as in the Figure 5c antigen-density simulations), following the same
  convention as the anti-BCMA CAR-T model `Su`'s predecessor
  `Singh_2021_idecabtageneVicleucel_human`.
- **Body weight cancels from the clinical outputs.** The blood and bone-marrow
  volumes both scale as `wt/70` and the dose is per kg, so every reported output
  is independent of body weight (and hence of the AGE covariate). AGE is carried
  for fidelity to the published model structure.
- **Printed-equation vs. as-run-code discrepancies resolved toward the code.**
  Several Supplement 1 display equations carry transcription slips that the
  deposited Monolix code (Supplement 2) corrects, and the model files follow the
  code: Eqs. 26/42 print the free CD22 tumour antigen from the CD19 total (the
  code uses the CD22 total); Eqs. 32-33/48-49 drop the `+` before the
  double-target complex in the complex sum (the code adds all three); and
  Eqs. 48-49 divide the bone-marrow complex ratios by the blood CAR-T/tumour
  pools (the code divides by the bone-marrow pools). The clinical-model
  simulations reproduce Table S3 to within a few percent, confirming the code
  reading.
- **In-vitro killing models carry no residual error.** Table 1 reports between-
  replicate variability on the in-vitro killing potency but no residual-error
  magnitude, so the in-vitro observation (`viability`) is encoded with a
  fixed-zero additive error. The multiple-myeloma datasets report cytotoxicity
  (`100 - viability`); the models output viability and the figures above plot its
  complement.
- As of the 2026-11 literature check there is no correction notice for this
  article.
```
